findings:
MERGED RANKING. This is a read-only synthesis of diag_blame, diag_headroom and diag_mechanisms. Scratch outputs are under /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-louisvasseur-Downloads-scaleli-sota/ac6d4251-6384-4db6-8aba-a17e1917a2ab/scratchpad/joint/{diag_blame,diag_headroom,diag_mechanisms}/.

I re-checked two code facts in /Users/louisvasseur/Downloads/scaleli_sota/experimental/scaleli/include/splice/:
- make_plan (cost.hpp:601-615) puts every tier-1 unit in section A, then every FENCED bbytes in section B (b = a_end).
- fixed_point (cost.hpp:836-866) varies only the three P scalars. It breaks on `st.choice == fp.sel.choice` and rejects any move that does not pass `e2 + 10 < ed_sel`.
- The Seg16 kind field is 2 bits and all 4 values are used (layout.hpp:25-32: 0 = FENCED, 1-3 = DIRECT W1/2/4). A new mode needs a bit stolen from pre:6 or base:24.

COMMON ROOT CAUSE, agreed by all three diagnoses:
- G, T and V act at disjoint scales. T works at 12k-50k keys (endpoint chord, knots from the eps-PLA proxy). V works at the entry: 9.5x leaf headroom over cbar. G works only at the two ends of the key range, and only the root router feels it.
- On the hard data every segment is FENCED. FENCED has a fixed floor of 2 dependent lines plus 2 walks, because entries and data sit in different regions.
- The only part of J that G, T or V can move is overcap: fb 0.08, osm 0.29, planet 0.14, genome 0. Bytes are free (lambda = 0 at every chosen hard cell).
- So the small ablation results (histtree within 0.03 D, exc=0 = 0) are a property of the layout family, as Louis assumed, not of the data.
- The outer loop cannot iterate because Fit (T, G) and the candidate caches (V) are frozen before fixed_point runs.

HEADROOM on the hard sets (fb / osm / genome / planet): today E[D] is 4.52 / 4.61 / 4.43 / 4.28. The floor of 1 line plus 1 walk is about 2.33-2.38. Each gap breaks down as:
- second dependent line: about 1.0
- second walk (region B): 0.94-1.05
- overcap plus router child: 0-0.29
- compute constant: about 0.15

CONFLICTS RESOLVED
(a) DIRECT with a stash on clusters: diag_blame and diag_mechanisms call it dead; diag_headroom measures -0.43 osm and -0.46 planet.
- Both are right. It fails on fb (stash 0.52-0.64) and genome (stash 0.64 even at 262k knots). It pays on osm and planet (41% / 39% of keys DIRECT at today's K).
- Kept as H6, conditional on beating PAGED per segment. The cluster-redirect variant is folded into it, because PAGED already acts as a page-granular redirect.

(b) Per-entry co-location (diag_blame) and PAGED (diag_mechanisms) attack the same second walk. PAGED dominates on bytes and D where it was measured (fb, osm). Co-located FENCED stays as the per-segment fallback candidate, and both go into the same selection.

(c) FENCED overcap-targeted T training (headroom H3) is merged into J-trained T (H3 here). Under PAGED, T's gradient becomes page overload, which is measured: histtree vs PLA is +0.09 D on osm under PAGED against +0.019 under FENCED. This is the first measured sign that the components cooperate.

GAPS AND CAVEATS
- Unmeasured: PAGED on genome and planet, and anything under the shared-L2 simulation. All PAGED and co-location numbers use default walk and residency constants.
- Excluded costs: spill second-walk cost is assumed 2.44-2.9 D; metadata is about 0.1 B/key; tier-1 record misses beyond record_miss0 are not counted.
- PAGED header capacity: 61 u16 fences do not fit a 2-line header (56 slots). Use 60 data lines or a 3-line header.
- books spans 2^63, so its compact relative keys likely overflow u32 and PAGED must use fast lines there. stack stays DIRECT (PAGED 2.56 > 2.33).

Recommended order: H1 + H2 as one candidate family, then H8 (fair-ablation harness, needed to judge everything else), then H3, H4, H5, H7 trained jointly inside the H7 outer loop. Then H6 on osm and planet only.

hypotheses.mechanism:
Add a third per-segment candidate, PAGED, which puts G, T and V at the same 4 KiB page scale.
- T maps x to a slot in a run of pages.
- Each page holds an in-page fence header (V: virtual boundaries that give the exact line, plus per-segment slack alpha) and 60-62 data lines (248 keys fast, 310 compact).
- Keys stay in their predicted page (cumulative max plus a backward clamp inside the page).
- An overloaded page keeps C keys. G spills the rest to a co-located FENCED child, with the boundary key stored in the header.
- The header and the predicted W-line window are fetched under ONE walk. A window miss costs 1 more line in the same page.
- A resident key costs 1 walk + 1 line, against 2 walks + 2 lines in FENCED.
hypotheses.defect_fixed: make_plan (cost.hpp:601-615) puts entries in section A and data in section B, so every FENCED lookup pays a second walk (0.94-1.05 D, the largest single headroom term). G, T and V act at disjoint scales, so each one is absorbed by the others and every ablation looks free. Bytes have no use (lambda = 0).

hypotheses.mechanism:
Replace the eps-PLA knots and the endpoint chord with knots and slopes trained on the exact J.
- Local moves: shift a knot by +-2^i keys (or +-1/64 to 1/4 of the segment), split, merge, and per-segment slope multipliers m*(1 +- 2^-k).
- Option: the PLA's own intercept as a base offset.
- Each move is scored by the exact delta, min over candidates of (cand_cost + lambda*bytes), recomputed only for the 1-2 segments it touches.
- Start from the PLA knots. K1 stays fixed by the L2 budget, so knots migrate from smooth regions to page or group overload boundaries.
- Under PAGED or co-location, T's slope sets page overload (G's spill) and the slack V needs. Under FENCED the target is group overcap.

hypotheses.mechanism:
Make G's in-segment choice an optimised set instead of a fixed rule.
- Which keys or groups leave the primary layout (PAGED spill, co-location spill, cluster ranges) is chosen per page by the J delta: a knapsack that spills the largest or most clustered groups.
- Exceptions (router and segment ends) are chosen by J instead of the 2x-span rule, with no hard 64-per-end cap.
- Spilled cluster keys are removed from T's fit set (virtual holes), so T's slope fits the non-cluster density. V then sizes slack for the residual only.

hypotheses.mechanism:
A second DIRECT family:
- Keys are order-free within a line (the eq4 compare ignores order).
- With a 2-line window, a line's overflow goes to the next line. Keys that still do not fit go to a bounded stash (G): either a co-located FENCED or PAGED child reached by an overflow marker (a reserved key value or a per-line bit), or a sentinel redirect line (e.g. k[0] > k[3]) carrying a line_off.
- T re-fits the slope over the non-stashed mass. V picks alpha in {1/8 .. 1} and the window per segment.
- Each segment chooses among DIRECT+stash, PAGED, coloc FENCED and FENCED.
- The cluster-redirect variant is folded in here.
hypotheses.defect_fixed: DIRECT is a cumulative-max linear probe (DirectPlace, cost.hpp:318-324), so one cluster drags every later key (mode=direct +158 D fb, +251 osm). G and V cannot trade with T inside DIRECT, and the mode is all-or-nothing per segment.

- Refuted for fb and genome: stash share 0.52-0.64 for any alpha and window, and no fb segment under a 30% stash.
On top of H1 the fallback is cheaper but the baseline is lower too: about -0.1 to -0.3 on osm and planet, 0 on fb and genome.

hypotheses.mechanism:
Turn fixed_point into an alternating loop over the components. Each iteration:
(a) select with the simulated per-region P.
(b) walk the plan and rank segments by marginal J (lines + walks x P, spill, overcap).
(c) G: re-choose the spill and stash set and exceptions (H4) for the top segments; spilled keys become virtual holes in T's fit set.
(d) T: run H3 moves on those segments against the new targets.
(e) V: re-pick alpha, cbar, k and W (H5).
(f) re-evaluate only the invalidated per-segment Sum caches, then re-select.
Stop when J falls by <= 0.01 D or the plan hash repeats.
hypotheses.defect_fixed: fixed_point (cost.hpp:836-866) varies only P. Fit and the candidate caches are frozen before it runs (build.hpp:179-190; splice_count 267-273). The synthesis states this by design ('no G/T/V alternation', splice_synthesis.md section 2 item 4).

Define neutral values and re-optimise the other two components on J, re-running the full grid (K1, entry, cbar, compact, mode, alpha) and the fixed point.
- T neutral: equi-width knots in key space, chord slope, no moves.
- G neutral: no exceptions, in-order spill, no stash or redirect, no virtual holes.
- V neutral: one global alpha/cbar, k = 1 (no co-location slack), fixed W.
Report the delta against the jointly optimised result per hard window and on average.
